B3DB_Classification.label_rule: TDC binary BBB penetration/permeability label Y

BBB_Martins.label_rule: TDC binary BBB penetration/permeability label Y

delta_sensitivity.selection_rule: Smallest evaluated margin with mean non-overlap B3DB external coverage >= 0.90; if none, highest mean coverage.

leakage_audit.policy: B3DB external test folds exclude exact canonical-SMILES overlaps with the full BBB Martins corpus when this preserves both classes; internal splits are audited for exact-SMILES, Murcko-scaffold, and Morgan-fingerprint maximum Tanimoto overlap against training rows.

notes: All analyses use checksum-identified public molecular data snapshots described in data_manifest.json.
No synthetic molecules, random labels, CIFAR/MNIST, or unrelated benchmark data are used.
Conformal sets use split conformal calibration; NeuroTx-MOOD variants use Mondrian/context quantiles.
BBB external validation uses the real B3DB classification benchmark with exact canonical-SMILES overlaps against BBB Martins removed where class diversity is preserved.
The experiment includes formal exact-SMILES, Murcko-scaffold, and Morgan-Tanimoto leakage audits against training rows.
Strong baselines now include a Morgan-fingerprint MLP and, when available, a frozen ChemBERTa molecular-transformer embedding with logistic regression.
Foundation-model benchmarking also includes a frozen IBM MoLFormer-XL molecular-transformer embedding with logistic regression under the same leakage-audited folds.
Context robustness is evaluated over basic and richer descriptor-bin Mondrian groups and minimum group sizes of 10, 25, and 50.
Delta sensitivity evaluates margins [0.0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.35, 0.4]; selected diagnostic delta is 0.30 under the recorded coverage-efficiency rule.
The OOD-guarded NeuroTx-MOOD variant applies a fixed +0.30 nonconformity margin to calibration quantiles before external evaluation; the margin is not fitted on B3DB labels.

A similarity-triggered guard analysis applies the same margin only to molecules below calibration-derived train-similarity thresholds, testing a lower-throughput-cost deployment policy without using external labels to set the trigger.
The ChEMBL CNS panel is additionally evaluated with a retrospective temporal split to provide a stronger prospective-like stress test than a pure random split.
Additional ChEMBL robustness analyses evaluate partial assay-metadata dropout and hierarchical assay grouping to probe sensitivity to metadata quality and grouping granularity.
ChEMBL validation uses compound-grouped random splits and compound-purged target/temporal evaluations.

primary_metric.name: external B3DB AUROC for NeuroTx-MOOD context-aware conformal RF

selective_guard.selection_rule: Retrospective utility screen over calibration-only similarity-quantile triggers; utility = success_rate - 0.25 * (mean_set_size - 1). Thresholds are derived from the calibration fold max-train-similarity distribution only.
